# pi-pii-redact

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact?logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact?logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact)
[![CI](https://github.com/chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

A [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) extension that keeps personally identifiable information (PII) and secrets away from the LLM.

Names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, card numbers, government IDs, API keys and more are replaced with stable tokens such as `[EMAIL_3#k7q2]` before anything is sent to the model. When the model uses those tokens in a tool call or a reply, the extension swaps the real values back in, so your tools still work on real data and you still read real values.

Detection runs locally with the [`@desert-ant-labs/redact`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@desert-ant-labs/redact) multilingual NER model plus regex rules. Nothing is sent to a third-party service for redaction.

## Installation

Requires [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) and Node.js 22 or later.

```bash
pi install npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact
```

This adds the package to your personal Pi settings (`~/.pi/agent/settings.json`), so it loads in every session. Start Pi as usual; the footer shows `PII: On` and redaction is active from the first prompt. Run `/pii status` to confirm.

> On first use the redaction model (about 25 MB) is downloaded from Hugging Face and cached in `~/.cache/desert-ant-models`, so the first session takes a moment longer to start.

### Other ways to install

| Goal | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Try it for one session without installing | `pi -e npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact` |
| Install for the current project only (`.pi/settings.json`) | `pi install -l npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact` |
| Pin a specific version | `pi install npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact@0.2.0` |
| Install from GitHub | `pi install git:github.com/chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact` |
| Install a local checkout | `pi install /path/to/pi-pii-redact` |

Project installs load only after you grant the project trust in Pi.

### Update and remove

```bash
pi update npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact   # update this package (pinned versions stay pinned)
pi update --extensions                  # update all installed packages
pi remove npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact   # uninstall
pi list                                 # show installed packages
```

## Example

You type:

```text
Email jane.doe@example.com that her card 4111 1111 1111 1111 was charged.
```

The model sees:

```text
Email [EMAIL_1#k7q2] that her card [CREDIT_CARD_1#k7q2] was charged.
```

If the model then calls a tool with `[EMAIL_1#k7q2]` as an argument, the tool receives `jane.doe@example.com`. Its reply is shown and stored with the real values.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `/pii` or `/pii status` | Show whether redaction is active and how many rules are enabled. |
| `/pii toggle` | Turn redaction on or off. |
| `/pii enable` / `/pii disable` | Turn redaction on or off explicitly. |
| `/pii rules` | List all rules and whether each is enabled. |

The enabled state and disabled rules are stored in the session and survive reloads.

## What gets redacted

| Group | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| People | given names, surnames |
| Addresses | street names, building numbers, apartment/suite, cities, states/provinces, ZIP/postal codes |
| Contact | email addresses, phone numbers, URLs, IP addresses |
| Financial | credit card numbers, bank account numbers, routing numbers, tax IDs |
| Government IDs | national IDs, SSNs, passports, driver's licenses |
| Devices | IMEI numbers |
| Secrets | API keys and tokens (`sk-…`, GitHub `ghp_…`/`gho_…`/…, GitLab `glpat-…`, AWS `AKIA…`) |
| Organizations | company and project names (**disabled by default** to avoid over-redacting code and docs) |

## Where redaction happens

| Pi event | What the extension does |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | Redacts your prompt before skill or prompt-template expansion. |
| `tool_result` | Redacts tool output (stdout, file contents, API responses, `structuredContent`) before it enters the conversation. |
| `context` | Re-redacts the whole history before every provider request: user and assistant text, tool-call arguments, tool results, bash executions, compaction and branch summaries. Messages are copied, never mutated. Assistant `thinking` blocks are left byte-identical because providers sign them. |
| `tool_call` | Restores tokens in tool arguments to the real values. |
| `message_end` | Restores tokens in the assistant reply so it is stored as plaintext. |
| compaction / branch summary | Both call the model directly, so the extension runs them itself with redacted input. If that is impossible (no model, auth failure, error) the summary is cancelled rather than falling back to plaintext. |

While a reply is streaming you may briefly see tokens; they are replaced with the real values when the message ends.

## How tokens work: the session vault

Each session has a vault that maps every sensitive value to a token such as `[EMAIL_3#k7q2]`:

- The same value always gets the same token, and the number per label only goes up, so the model sees consistent identities across turns.
- `k7q2` is a random per-session nonce. Text that merely looks like a token (for example `[EMAIL_1]` in a file) is never restored.
- Restore tolerates the ways models mangle tokens: missing brackets, lower case and extra spaces (`email_3#k7q2`, `[ EMAIL_3 # k7q2 ]`). Tokens not in the vault are left unchanged.
- Rules with a custom `mask` are one-way and are not restored.

## Security model

This extension protects **what reaches the model**, not what is on disk.

| Data | In the session file | Sent to the LLM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your input, tool output | redacted (tokens) | tokens |
| Assistant replies, tool-call arguments, compaction and branch summaries | **plaintext** (restored) | re-redacted to tokens by `context` |
| Vault mapping | `pii-vault` custom entries with token and original | never |

**Session files contain the original values**, both in the `pii-vault` entries and in assistant replies. Protect them like any other file holding sensitive data.

input.prompt:
Repo: /home/ubuntu/.t3/worktrees/pi-pii-redact/t3-de72474e (a git worktree; work only here, do not commit). It is a Pi coding-agent extension (`@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact`) that redacts PII into vault tokens like `[EMAIL_3#k7q2]` and restores them. node_modules is installed. Validate with `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` (both must pass).

## Goal
Add a usage board: a new `/pii stats` subcommand showing how much PII was redacted/restored.

## Relevant files (already reviewed by me)
- src/commands/pii.ts — `/pii` command (status/toggle/rules/enable/disable). Add `stats` here and to `getArgumentCompletions`; update command description to "Manage PII redaction (status, toggle, rules, stats)" (and update the test in tests/commands.test.ts 1.2 that asserts the description).
- src/hooks/index.ts — all event hooks. `counter()` helper wraps `redactor.redact` and sums `result.count`; `restore` wraps `redactor.restore`.
- src/services/vault.ts — `PiiVault`; `restore(text)` uses tolerantRegex; `knownOriginals()` returns entries with `label` (e.g. EMAIL, GIVEN_NAME); `size`.
- src/services/redactor.ts — `RedactorService` (`redact()` returns `RedactionResult` with `redactions: RedactionDetail[]`, each has `category`, `masked`), `getVault()`, `getRules()`, `isEnabled()`.
- src/index.ts — wires `registerHooks(pi, redactor)` and `registerPiiCommands(pi, redactor)`.
- tests/mock-pi.ts, tests/commands.test.ts, tests/hooks.test.ts — test mocks/patterns.
- Pi UI API: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts (`ctx.ui.custom`, `ctx.hasUI`, `Theme`). Example of an overlay component: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples/extensions/todo.ts (uses `matchesKey`, `truncateToWidth` from `@earendil-works/pi-tui`, `theme.fg("dim"|"muted"|"accent"|"success"|"text", ...)`, `theme.bold`, closes on escape/ctrl+c via `done()`).

## Design (decided — follow it)
1. New `src/services/stats.ts` with a `PiiStats` class, in-memory counters for the current Pi process ("this run"; they reset on restart/reload — that's accepted):
   - redactions by source: `input` (items + number of prompts that had redactions), `tool` (items, broken down by tool name), `summary` (compaction + branch summary items/count).
   - redactions by category (from `RedactionDetail.category`).
   - context: number of `context` requests that changed messages, and items re-masked there. Context items must NOT be added to the headline "redacted" total or the category breakdown (the context hook re-redacts the whole history every turn, so it would massively overcount). 
   - restores: tokens restored in tool-call args and in assistant replies (separate counters).
   - a `snapshot()` returning plain data; a `reset()` is fine but not required.
   Create one instance in src/index.ts and pass it to both `registerHooks` and `registerPiiCommands` (add a param; keep it optional with a default `new PiiStats()` if that keeps existing tests/call sites simple).
2. Counting restores: extend `PiiVault.restore(text, onHit?: (entry: VaultEntry) => void)` (call only for actually-restored tokens) and `RedactorService.restore(text, onHit?)` passthrough. Don't change behavior otherwise.
3. Hooks: extend `counter()` to also collect the `redactions` details so callers can record categories. Record in `input`, `tool_result` (use `event.toolName`, fallback "unknown"), `context`, `session_before_compact`, `session_before_tree`, `tool_call`, `message_end`. Only record when redaction actually happened (count > 0).
4. Persistent section from the vault: unique protected values in this session, grouped by vault `label` (survives reloads since the vault is rebuilt from session entries). Compute in the board from `redactor.getVault().knownOriginals()` — never display original values or tokens, only counts per label.
5. Board rendering: put a pure function `renderStatsLines(data, opts)` (e.g. in src/commands/stats-board.ts) that produces lines, with an optional theme-ish styling hook so the same function serves both the TUI overlay and a plain-text fallback. Content, roughly:
   ```
   PII redaction usage
   Status: ON · 23/24 rules enabled
   
   Protected values this session: 14
     email        ██████████ 5
     given name   ██████ 3
     ...
   Redacted this run: 37
     Prompts       12  (4 prompts)
     Tool output   25  (bash 18, read 7)
     Summaries      0
   Top categories this run
     email  ███ 10 ...
   Restored to real values: 9  (tool args 6, replies 3)
   Context: 41 requests re-masked (52 items)
   ```
   Category names displayed humanized: lowercase, `_`/`-` → space (so vault label GIVEN_NAME and category variants render the same). Sort breakdowns by count desc; bars scaled to the max in that block; show a friendly "nothing yet" line for empty blocks. Truncate every line to width.
6. `/pii stats`: if `ctx.hasUI` and `ctx.ui.custom` exists, open an overlay component (`ctx.ui.custom<void>(..., { overlay: true })`) with a footer hint "Esc to close", closing on escape/ctrl+c/q; otherwise `ctx.ui.notify(lines.join("\n"), "info")` with plain lines.
   `@earendil-works/pi-tui` is installed but not declared: add it to `peerDependencies` as `"*"` (like the other pi packages) and to devDependencies at the version present in node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/package.json (`^x.y.z`), then run `npm install` to update package-lock.json.
7. Docs: add `/pii stats` row to README's Commands table (one line, note the "this run" counters reset when Pi restarts while protected-value counts come from the session vault). Add a changeset file `.changeset/pii-stats-board.md`: `---\n"@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact": minor\n---\n\nAdd `/pii stats` usage board ...`.

## Tests (required)
- tests/stats.test.ts: PiiStats counting, context not inflating totals, renderStatsLines output (empty state, humanized labels, ordering, no originals/tokens appear in output, width truncation).
- vault: `restore` onHit called once per restored token, not for unknown/foreign tokens.
- hooks: using existing mock patterns, an input with redactions and a tool_result increment the right counters; tool_call/message_end restores counted.
- commands: `/pii stats` completion present; with `hasUI` false it notifies text; with `hasUI` true it calls `ui.custom` (mock it in tests/mock-pi.ts if needed).
Keep code style consistent with the repo (2-space, double quotes, short JSDoc comments). Don't refactor unrelated code. Report the files changed and test/typecheck results.

The full suite has 4 failures: perf tests that time out while running the real detection model on large inputs. I couldn't confirm they also fail on `main`, because my baseline run was stopped at its 15-minute limit before it printed anything. What it counts:
- **Protected values this session:** the number of different sensitive values in the session's token list, grouped by type. This survives restarts and resumes because it's rebuilt from the session file. It shows counts only, never the values or tokens.
- **This-run counters:** what was redacted from your prompts, from tool output (split by tool) and from summaries, by type, plus how many tokens were swapped back to real values. They're kept in memory and reset when Pi restarts.
- **Context re-masking is shown on its own line** and isn't added to the totals. Before every model request the extension re-redacts the whole conversation, so adding those would inflate the numbers on every turn.

In Pi's terminal UI it opens as a popup that closes with Esc or `q`. Without the UI it prints the same board as plain text.

The new code is in `src/services/stats.ts` (counters) and `src/commands/stats-board.ts` (layout). The rest of the change:
- **Hooks and command:** the counting is wired into `src/hooks/index.ts` and the command into `src/commands/pii.ts`.
- **Counting restores:** the vault's `restore` can now report each token it swaps back.
- **Package:** `@earendil-works/pi-tui` (Pi's terminal UI library) is now a peer dependency, `*`, like the other Pi packages.
- **Docs and release:** a row in the README's command table and a minor changeset.
- **Tests:** new `tests/stats.test.ts`, plus new cases in the vault, hooks and commands tests.

Base directory for this skill: /home/ubuntu/.claude/skills/sol-loop

# sol-loop

This is a workflow for making your code changes more correct before (or
sometimes after) filing a pull request. tl;dr - use OpenAI's GPT Sol to review
your code in a loop.

Make the most minimal possible changes to appease the Sol reviewers. Be careful
of scope creep and don't be scared to push back.

## Budget

- Default: 3 rounds total. Round 1 is full. Later rounds check only
  changed code and open findings.
- Extend to 5 only for security, permissions, auth, data loss, or
  state/concurrency, while a blocker or should stays open with evidence. Or when
  the user asks.
- Stop early if a round returns only nits. Declined nits and comment,
  doc, or format-only fixes need no new round.
- One reviewer only. Sol must not start subagents or reviewers.
- Keep a ledger: id, severity, outcome, usage if returned. Never guess it.

## 1. Scope

Run `git status --short`. Do not stash, discard, or include unrelated
changes. Limit review to the change paths if they separate cleanly.
Otherwise stop and ask.

Find the base after `git fetch origin`:

- PR: `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName,headRefOid`. Check out the branch
  only if clean. Confirm `HEAD` is the PR head, or ahead only by this
  change. Base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`.
- Local: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>`. No remote: a base
  the user names, or `HEAD` for uncommitted changes only.

The change is base to working tree in those paths, with untracked files.
Use one diff command all rounds. State intent and out-of-scope in 1-2
sentences. Run covering checks. Do not send code this change breaks. Note
missing or pre-failing checks in the brief.

## 2. Start Sol

In T3, call `orchestrator_capabilities`. Pick the latest Sol unless the user
named a version. Do not hardcode an ID. Record provider, model, and effort
only if exposed. Use `delegate_task` every round (`role: "review"`,
`mode: "async"`). Save `taskId`. New `clientRequestId` per round.
`childThreadId` is storage, not the next target. Do not use
`t3_thread_send`, `create_threads`, or `t3_thread_launch` for review.

If T3 tools are not listed, try one direct capability call. Outside T3, use
a native Sol subagent and keep its ID. In Claude Code, use a custom subagent
only if it is set up to run Sol. If no route runs Sol, report the blocker. Do
not substitute a model.

Do not edit scoped files while review runs. Wait for the notice. Do not
poll or start a second reviewer. Timeout, error, or no reply is not
approval. On failure, cancel, verify stop, restart with the ledger.

Round 1 brief (T3 children get no history):

```
Review only. Do not edit, commit, push, comment on PRs, or start subagents.
Repo: <abs path> Base: <sha> Intent: <intent> Out of scope: <scope> Checks: <results>
See: git diff <base> [-- <paths>]; git status --short (read untracked).
Read surrounding code. Find bugs, broken callers, mismatch with intent.
Skip style unless it hides a bug. Hold to the smallest change. Flag code,
tests, or guards the intent does not need. Other paths, rare cases, small
perf, extra compat: nits.
blocker = intended case wrong. should = real bug callers will hit, in intent. nit = rest.
Reply:
VERDICT: APPROVE or CHANGES
S1 [blocker|should|nit] <file>:<line> <claim>. Fix: <suggestion> (stable ids)
```

## 3. Answer findings

Check each finding and severity yourself. Another path, rare case, or
small cost is a nit, whatever label it came with.

- Agree: smallest fix. Prefer delete or narrow over new lock, cache,
  helper, or option. Fix the case that happened. Add one focused test
  that fails without the fix, if intent needs it.
- Disagree: say why, with evidence (file:line, test, output).
- Out of scope or nit: decline in one line. List as follow-up.

Update the ledger. Re-run checks and `git diff --shortstat <base>`. If
review grew the diff, cut first. Do not agree just to end the loop.

## 4. Next round

Start one only if budget remains and a blocker or should is open, behavior code
changed, or approval does not cover the current behavior diff. Use a fresh
`delegate_task` in T3, or follow up the saved native ID. Send the round 1 brief,
the ledger (`fixed:` / `disagree:` / `declined:` + evidence), the same base
diff, and the change since last round. Tell Sol: open ids and changed code only.
Mark each old id `resolved` or `still open: <reason>`.

## 5. Stop and ship

Agreed: APPROVE on the current behavior diff, no blocker or should open,
no concern of your own. Stuck: an item stays disputed after two replies,
or budget ends. Show both sides in 2-3 lines each. The user decides.
Budget end is not approval.

Do not push during the loop. Push after agreement only if the user asked
to push, ship, or update the PR. If you push to a PR, add above the model
blurb:

`Reviewed with sol-loop: <N> rounds with <model>. Sol verdict: approved`.

Add `on <effort>` only if verified.

Report: rounds, model, what Sol changed, diff size before/after, fixed and
declined findings with reasons, usage if exposed (else say not), pushed or not.

# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to coding agents working with code in this repository.

## What this is

A [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) extension (published as `@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact`) that replaces PII and secrets with stable per-session tokens like `[EMAIL_3#k7q2]` before anything reaches the LLM, and restores real values in tool-call arguments and assistant replies. Detection runs locally: the `@desert-ant-labs/redact` NER model plus regex overlay rules.

The package ships TypeScript source directly (`main` and `pi.extensions` point at `src/index.ts`); there is no build step.

## Commands

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck                         # tsc --noEmit (covers src/ only)
npm test                                  # vitest run, all suites
npx vitest run tests/vault.test.ts        # one file
npx vitest run tests/e2e                  # e2e tiers only
npx vitest run -t "restores tokens"       # tests matching a name
pi -e .                                   # load the working copy into Pi
```

Most tests run the real on-device model on CPU. On first run it downloads (~25 MB) into `~/.cache/desert-ant-models`. `vitest.config.ts` sets a 30 s timeout and `fileParallelism: false` on purpose, because parallel files each load a model and oversubscribe the CPU. Don't change those to speed things up.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs typecheck and tests on Node 22 and 24.

## Architecture

`src/index.ts` creates one `RedactorService` and passes it to `registerHooks` (`src/hooks/index.ts`) and `registerPiiCommands` (`src/commands/pii.ts`).

**`RedactorService` (`src/services/redactor.ts`)** owns the rules, the config, the lazily loaded native model, an LRU result cache and the session vault. `redact()` runs in this order:
1. Splits enabled rules into regex overlay rules (those with a `pattern`) and native model labels.
2. Fast path: replaces originals already in the vault with their tokens.
3. Applies the regex overlays. `replaceOutsideTokens` never touches text overlapping an existing vault token.
4. Runs native inference for the active labels, filtered by `minimumConfidence` (default 0.85).

Anything that changes rules, the enabled state or the vault must clear the cache, as the existing setters do.

**`PiiVault` (`src/services/vault.ts`)** is the two-way map between originals and tokens. The same original always gets the same token. Per-label counters only increase. A random per-vault nonce means text that merely looks like a token is never restored. Restore tolerates mangled tokens (lower case, missing brackets, extra spaces). Rules with a custom `mask` are one-way and never enter the vault.

**Rules (`src/rules/default-rules.ts`)**: `MODEL_RULE_DEFINITIONS` maps the 22 native labels to `PiiRule`s (`ORG` is disabled by default), plus the regex overlays for API keys and similar. `toggleRule` accepts ids, native labels and aliases.

**Hooks (`src/hooks/index.ts`)** handle the Pi events:
- Redaction: `input`, `tool_result` (including `structuredContent`) and `context`. `context` re-redacts the whole history before every provider request.
- Restore: `tool_call` restores arguments in place, and `message_end` restores the assistant reply. Both run even while redaction is off, as long as the vault has entries.
- `session_before_compact` / `session_before_tree`: these call the model directly and bypass `context`, so the extension runs `compact` / `generateBranchSummary` itself on redacted input. **On any failure they return `{ cancel: true }`** and never fall back to plaintext.
- `session_start` rebuilds the vault and config from session entries. `session_shutdown` disposes the model.

**Message walkers (`src/hooks/messages.ts`)** deep-map strings through messages and content blocks. Invariants: never mutate the input, return the *same reference* when nothing changed (hooks use reference equality to decide whether to return a result), and leave assistant `thinking` blocks byte-identical because providers sign them.

**Persistence (`src/hooks/persist.ts`)**: state lives in session custom entries. `pii-vault` entries are append-only deltas from `vault.takePendingDelta()`. Call `persistVaultDelta` after any redaction that may have minted tokens. The vault is rebuilt from *all* entries across branches so numbers are never reused. `pii-config` holds the latest enabled state plus disabled rule ids. Session files therefore contain plaintext originals by design; the extension protects what reaches the model, not what is on disk.

## Tests

- `tests/mock-pi.ts` provides `createMockExtensionAPI` (captures handlers and `appendEntry` as session entries), `createMockContext` and `createMockRedactor` (no model) for unit tests.
- `tests/e2e/harness.ts` provides `PiTestHarness` for opaque-box tests through the public entry points, plus `assertRedacted*` matchers. The tiers cover features, boundaries, combinations, workflows and adversarial cases (`tier1` to `tier5`). The core assertion is that the original value is absent from the output and a placeholder is present.
- `TEST_INFRA.md` / `TEST_READY.md` describe the e2e methodology. They reference `ORIGINAL_REQUEST.md` / `PROJECT.md`, which are not in the repo.

## Releasing

Use Changesets. Any PR that changes behavior needs a changeset (`npx changeset`, committed in `.changeset/`). Merging to `main` opens a "Version Packages" PR, and merging that publishes to npm via OIDC trusted publishing (`.github/workflows/publish.yml`). Don't hand-edit the `version` in `package.json` or `CHANGELOG.md`.
